skill.name: better-interface

skill.summary: Coordinates six specialist interface reviews into one evidence-based report ranked by user impact.

content.user_title: Review Interfaces Across Six Design Disciplines
content.value_statement: Separate interface reviews can duplicate issues and obscure the most important fixes. This skill coordinates specialist reviews into one evidence-based report ranked by user impact.
actual_capabilities: Coordinates available specialist skills for accessibility, layout, writing, typography, color, and UI polish.
Defines review scope, project conventions, and coverage across relevant interface states.
Consolidates shared root causes into one ranked table with at most 15 findings.
Requires implementation evidence and relevant rendered checks before making interface claims.
Prioritizes fixes using native controls, existing project patterns, and minimal changes.
Reports verification results, unreviewed domains, and an Approve or Block verdict.
limitations: The six specialist skills are separate dependencies; unavailable domains must be marked Not reviewed.
Branch, pull request, commit range, and uncommitted change reviews require the user to invoke interface-review.
Runtime and visual verification depend on available previews, tools, and project checks.
Reviews are read-only unless implementation is requested, and approval covers only inspected domains.

use_cases.title: Prioritize frontend fixes
use_cases.description: Review a complete application flow and consolidate repeated component issues into actionable fixes ranked by user impact.

use_cases.title: Check design consistency
use_cases.description: Compare an implemented screen with project conventions across typography, color, layout, writing, and accessibility.

use_cases.title: Assess release readiness
use_cases.description: Review a critical user journey with explicit coverage, verification results, and a verdict based on remaining high-impact issues.

prompt_templates.title: Review one screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [screen] with better-interface. Keep the review read-only and return ranked findings, coverage, verification, and a verdict.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: request a focused interface review.

prompt_templates.title: Review a complete flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [flow] across all available domains. Include empty, loading, error, and narrow-width states, and state any excluded surfaces.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: examine a journey across multiple states.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate shared issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [feature] using our documented design conventions. Consolidate repeated issues against shared tokens or components and prioritize the smallest effective fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: identify systemic causes without imposing a new stack.

prompt_templates.title: Review and implement fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [flow] and implement the consolidated findings within that scope. Use project-native solutions, rerun relevant checks, and report remaining issues and unverified behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: explicitly authorize implementation and follow-up verification.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: review a settings screen where rendered testing confirms the close control has no accessible name.
output: Scope: settings screen and its close control.
HIGH, Accessibility: the close control has no accessible name. Add a name that describes its action.
Verification: rendered accessibility inspection confirms the missing name.
Verdict: Block until the high-impact finding is resolved; name any unreviewed domains.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: summarize a review with no actionable findings where the writing skill was unavailable.
output: Coverage: list the files, components, states, and checks inspected for each completed domain.
Writing: Not reviewed because better-writing was unavailable.
Verdict: Approve for inspected domains only. Writing was not reviewed.

best_practices: Specify one complete screen or flow and provide the relevant project conventions.
Make specialist skills and a working preview available before requesting broad coverage.
Check the evidence, verification results, and unreviewed domains before relying on an approval.
anti_patterns: Treating missing specialist skills or unverified checks as proof that a domain passed.
Requesting repository-wide coverage when the available context supports only one complete flow.
Expecting source edits from a review request without explicitly authorizing implementation.

faq.question: Which AI tools are listed as supported?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Available checks and specialist skill loading depend on the host environment.

faq.question: Does this package include all six specialist skills?
faq.answer: No. It references better-accessibility, better-layout, better-writing, better-typography, better-colors, and better-ui. Missing domains must be marked Not reviewed.

faq.question: Will a review change my source files?
faq.answer: No, reviews are read-only by default. Source changes require an explicit implementation request.

faq.question: Can it review a pull request directly?
faq.answer: It directs change-scoped requests to interface-review, which the user must invoke. It can consolidate a review handed back by that skill.

faq.question: What does an Approve verdict mean?
faq.answer: No HIGH findings remain within inspected domains. MEDIUM and LOW findings may remain, and unreviewed domains must be named.

faq.question: Does it guarantee accessibility compliance?
faq.answer: No. Results depend on specialist rules, inspected evidence, and available verification. Unavailable checks and unreviewed domains must be disclosed.
